The core insight is a duality between control and trust in managed leagues. Control (C) and trust (T) form a value proposition V = C ⊕ T, where ⊕ denotes a non-linear combination. This duality implies that users cannot simultaneously maximize both C and T in traditional systems—hence, advisor apps offer C but not T, while concierge services offer T but not C. The gap is filled by the GM Autopilot, which allows delegation while preserving visibility. Each action is recorded in a tamper-evident ledger (\mathcal{L}), ensuring that AI behavior is accountable. The delegation dial D maps user intent to agent autonomy, with explanations, reversibility, and learning embedded. Failure modes include: (1) when D=1, opacity risks emerge; (2) when \mathcal{L} is incomplete, trust erodes; (3) when C and T are misaligned, value collapses. The system's robustness depends on maintaining this balance through structured feedback loops.
